arxiv-1807-01808.title: Discrete Sampling using Semigradient-based Product Mixtures
arxiv-1807-01808.creator: Alkis Gotovos, Hamed Hassani, Andreas Krause, Stefanie Jegelka
arxiv-1807-01808.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Alkis Gotovos, Hamed Hassani, Andreas Krause, Stefanie Jegelka. We consider the problem of inference in discrete probabilistic models, that is, distributions over subsets of a finite ground set. These encompass a range of well-known models in machine learning, such as determinantal point processes and Ising models. Locally-moving Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms, such as the Gibbs sampler, are commonly used for inference in such models, but their convergence is, at times, prohibitively slow.

arxiv-2012-06811.description: Abstract . Let Y Y be an integral nodal projective curve of arithmetic genus g ≥ 2 g\geq 2 with m m nodes defined over an algebraically closed field k k and x x a nonsingular closed point of Y Y . Let n n and d d be coprime integers with n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 .

arxiv-2107-14198.title: Twist structures and Nelson conuclei
arxiv-2107-14198.creator: Manuela Busaniche and Nikolaos Galatos and Miguel Marcos
arxiv-2107-14198.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manuela Busaniche and Nikolaos Galatos and Miguel Marcos. Motivated by Kalman residuated lattices, Nelson residuated lattices and Nelson paraconsistent residuated lattices, we provide a natural common generalization of them. Nelson conucleus algebras unify these examples and further extend them to the non-commutative setting. We study their structure, establish a representation theorem for them in terms of twist structures and conuclei that results in a categorical adjunction, and explore situations where the representation is actually an isomorphism.

arxiv-2206-05051.title: Temporal Inductive Logic Reasoning over Hypergraphs Note: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-24)
arxiv-2206-05051.creator: Yuan Yang, Siheng Xiong, Ali Payani, James C. Kerce, Faramarz Fekri
arxiv-2206-05051.description: Abstract Inductive logic reasoning is a fundamental task in graph analysis, which aims to generalize patterns from data. This task has been extensively studied for traditional graph representations, such as knowledge graphs (KGs), using techniques like inductive logic programming (ILP). Existing ILP methods assume learning from KGs with static facts and binary relations.

arxiv-2208-12220.title: On adiabatic theory for extended fermionic lattice systems
arxiv-2208-12220.creator: Joscha Henheik, Tom Wessel
arxiv-2208-12220.description: Abstract We review recent results on adiabatic theory for ground states of extended gapped fermionic lattice systems under several different assumptions. More precisely, we present generalized super-adiabatic theorems for extended but finite and infinite systems, assuming either a uniform gap or a gap in the bulk above the unperturbed ground state.

arxiv-2208-13076.title: Pressure-robust enriched Galerkin methods for the Stokes equations Submitted to Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics in 2023.
arxiv-2208-13076.creator: Xiaozhe Hu, Seulip Lee, Lin Mu, Son-Young Yi
arxiv-2208-13076.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a pressure-robust enriched Galerkin (EG) scheme for solving the Stokes equations, which is an enhanced version of the EG scheme for the Stokes problem proposed in [S.-Y. Yi, X. Hu, S. Lee, J. H. Adler, An enriched Galerkin method for the Stokes equations, Computers and Mathematics with Applications 120 (2022) 115–131].

arxiv-2406-14833.title: Efficient Continual Pre-training by Mitigating the Stability Gap
arxiv-2406-14833.creator: Yiduo Guo, Jie Fu, Huishuai Zhang, Dongyan Zhao, Yikang shen
arxiv-2406-14833.description: Abstract Continual pre-training has increasingly become the predominant approach for adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to new domains. This process involves updating the pre-trained LLM with a corpus from a new domain, resulting in a shift in the training distribution. To study the behavior of LLMs during this shift, we measured the model’s performance throughout the continual pre-training process.

arxiv-2410-18832.title: MazeNet: An Accurate, Fast, & Scalable Deep Learning Solution For Steiner Minimum Trees
arxiv-2410-18832.creator: Gabriel Díaz RamosRice University gd27@rice.edu, Toros ArikanRice University toros@rice.edu, Richard G. BaraniukRice University richb@rice.edu
arxiv-2410-18832.description: Abstract The Obstacle Avoiding Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree (OARSMT) problem, which seeks the shortest interconnection of a given number of terminals in a rectilinear plane while avoiding obstacles, is a critical task in integrated circuit design, network optimization, and robot path planning.

arxiv-2501-06887.title: MedGrad E-CLIP: Enhancing Trust and Transparency in AI-Driven Skin Lesion Diagnosis
arxiv-2501-06887.creator: Sadia Kamal, Tim Oates
arxiv-2501-06887.description: Abstract As deep learning models gain attraction in medical data, ensuring transparent and trustworthy decision-making is essential. In skin cancer diagnosis, while advancements in lesion detection and classification have improved accuracy, the black-box nature of these methods poses challenges in understanding their decision processes, leading to trust issues among physicians.

arxiv-2503-20737.title: Ontology-based Semantic Similarity Measures for Clustering Medical Concepts in Drug Safety
arxiv-2503-20737.creator: Jeffery L. Painter, François Haguinet, Greg Powell, Andrew Bate
arxiv-2503-20737.description: Abstract Semantic similarity measures (SSMs) are widely used in biomedical research but remain underutilized in pharmacovigilance. This study evaluates six ontology-based SSMs for clustering MedDRA Preferred Terms (PTs) in drug safety data. Using the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS), we assess each method’s ability to group PTs around medically meaningful centroids.

arxiv-2506-08969.title: A New Spectral Class of Brown Dwarfs at the Bottom of the IMF in IC 348
arxiv-2506-08969.creator: K. L. Luhman, C. Alves de Oliveira
arxiv-2506-08969.description: Abstract In a previous study, we used JWST to identify three new brown dwarfs in the center of a nearby star-forming cluster, IC 348. The faintest object had an estimated mass of 3–4 M Jup M_{\rm Jup} , making it a contender for the least massive brown dwarf confirmed with spectroscopy.

arxiv-2511-18519.title: CHIPS: Efficient CLIP Adaptation via Curvature-aware Hybrid Influence-based Data Selection
arxiv-2511-18519.creator: Xinlin Zhuang, Yichen Li, Xiwei Liu, Haolin Yang, Yifan Lu, Ziyun Zou, Yulong Li, Huifa Li, Dongliang Chen, Qinglei Wang, Weiyang Liu, Ying Qian, Jiangming Shi, Imran Razzak
arxiv-2511-18519.description: Abstract Adapting CLIP to vertical domains is typically approached by novel fine-tuning strategies or by continual pre-training (CPT) on large domain-specific datasets. Yet, data itself remains an underexplored factor in this process. We revisit this task from a data-centric perspective: Can effective data selection substitute for large-scale datasets in CPT?

pmc-10689637.title: Next Generation PDE4 Inhibitors that Selectively Target PDE4B/D Subtypes: A Narrative Review
pmc-10689637.creator: Andrew Blauvelt, Richard G. Langley, Kenneth B. Gordon, Jonathan I. Silverberg, Kilian Eyerich, Morten O. A. Sommer, Jakob Felding, Richard B. Warren
pmc-10689637.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). For decades, topical corticosteroids have been the mainstay of treatment for mild-to-moderate inflammatory skin diseases, even though only short-term use is approved for these agents and systemic inflammation is not addressed. Increased understanding of the immunopathogenesis of these conditions, especially for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis, has facilitated the development of antibody-based drugs that neutralize single key cytokines or their associated receptors, such as interleukin (IL)-17A/F, IL-23, and IL-17RA in psoriasis and IL-13 and IL-4Rα in atopic dermatitis.

pmc-10703085.title: A target tracking method based on adaptive occlusion judgment and model updating strategy
pmc-10703085.creator: Zhiming Cai, Zhuangzhuang Wang, Jianchao Huang, Shujing Chen, Huabin He
pmc-10703085.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Target tracking is an important research in the field of computer vision. Despite the rapid development of technology, difficulties still remain in balancing the overall performance for target occlusion, motion blur, etc. To address the above issue, we propose an improved kernel correlation filter tracking algorithm with adaptive occlusion judgement and model updating strategy (called Aojmus) to achieve robust target tracking.

pmc-10707900.title: Radiation Curing of Phosphorus Telomer-Based Coatings Using UV LEDs or Medium-Pressure Mercury Lamp
pmc-10707900.creator: Agata Kraśkiewicz, Agnieszka Kowalczyk
pmc-10707900.description: In the presented study, UV LEDs (365 nm) or a medium-pressure mercury lamp (UV-ABC) were verified as UV radiation sources initiating the photocrosslinking process of varnishes based on novel photopolymerizable phosphorus (meth)acrylate oligomers. Coating formulations were composed of (meth)acrylic/styrene telomers with terminal P-atoms (prepared via a UV phototelomerization process) and different photoinitiators (HAPs, APOs, or APO blends).

pmc-11342515.title: Reliability and validity of the Chinese version of the coronary artery disease empowerment scale (CADES) in patients with coronary artery disease after percutaneous coronary intervention
pmc-11342515.creator: Zhili Jiang, Zhiqian Wang, Yang Liu, Wenxiao Wu, Ziying Dai, Yeyao Yang, Lihua Huang
pmc-11342515.description: BackgroundEmpowerment is a comprehensive concept involving intrapersonal, interactional, and behavioral aspects. However, there is a lack of a specific empowerment scale for Coronary artery disease (CAD) related to knowledge and skills in China. The reliability and validity of the Coronary Artery Disease Empowerment Scale (CADES) need to be tested.

pmc-11605809.title: Antecedent viral immunization and efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade: an extensive serum antibody profile to predict outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-11605809.creator: Filippo G Dall’Olio, Wael Salem Zrafi, Quentin Blampey, Francois-Xavier Danlos, Matthieu Roulleaux-Dugage, Gabriel Roman, Charles Naltet, Paul-Henry Cournède, Daniel Gautheret, Mihaela Aldea, David Planchard, Fabrice Barlesi, Aurelien Marabelle, Tyler Hulett, Nathalie Chaput-Gras, Benjamin Besse
pmc-11605809.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionImmune checkpoint blockers (ICBs) revolutionized the treatment of patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) but only a fraction of them obtain a response, and clinical benefit from these treatments is often difficult to predict.

pmc-11717139.title: Effect of Preoperative Corticosteroid Injections on Postoperative Risk of Periprosthetic Joint Infection and Revision Surgery After Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11717139.creator: Muzammil Akhtar, Daniel I Razick, Anand Dhaliwal, Kaitlyn Guadagno, Osamah Baig, Jimmy Wen, Mustafa Jundi, Dawnica Nadora, Denise Nadora, Eric Huish
pmc-11717139.description: In total joint arthroplasty, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) can be devastating. Corticosteroid injections (CSIs) are commonly administered for temporary pain relief in the setting of various conditions. Therefore, the current systematic review aims to evaluate whether CSIs administered prior to total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) are a risk factor for PJI and revision surgery.

pmc-12590683.title: Sleep quality during pregnancy: the role of anxiety, fear of childbirth, and obstetric factors – a multicenter cross-sectional study
pmc-12590683.creator: Mojdeh Banaei, Shiva Alizadeh, Nasibeh Roozbeh, Marzieh Saei Ghare-Naz, Elahe Taghvaei, Leila Parviz, Vida Ghasemi
pmc-12590683.description: BackgroundPregnancy is a vulnerable period for poor sleep quality, and sleep disturbances might increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. Therefore, the present study aimed to identify the prevalence of poor sleep quality and examine the association of pregnancy-related anxiety, fear of childbirth, sociodemographic and obstetric factors with sleep quality among Iranian pregnant women.

pmc-12720664.title: Oral Prevotella induces fat taste impairment, visceral lipid accumulation and insulin resistance by downregulating Hedgehog signaling in taste buds
pmc-12720664.creator: Xiaohuan Liu, Jiehan Zhang, Yi He, Qiao Zhang, Shuaixian Du, Tianshu Zeng, Jiaoyue Zhang, Hao Zhang, Han Luo, Huiqing Li, Ying Wang, Miaomiao Peng, Nan Zhang, Qi Chen, Hantao Huang, Ping Wang, Lulu Chen, Xiang Hu
pmc-12720664.description: BackgroundFat taste impairment has been implicated in visceral lipid accumulation and insulin resistance, with emerging evidence linking it to the oral microbiota. However, the role and mechanisms of the oral microbiota in this process remain unclear.ObjectiveWe aimed to explore the manifestations of Prevotella in fat taste, visceral lipid accumulation and insulin sensitivity, as well as to elucidate the mechanism involved.

pmc-12964671.title: The indirect associations of academic self-efficacy and brief fear of negative evaluation in the relationship between neurotic personality traits and test anxiety of medical sciences students
pmc-12964671.creator: Lv Lin, Yu Hongyu, Jiang Xing, Ma Ying, Liang Zixuan, Luan Tingting
pmc-12964671.description: BackgroundResearch on test anxiety has decreased in recent years, but the phenomenon of test anxiety has always been a major hazard that continuously plagues students’ academic performance. In recent years, with educational reforms, there have been more variables in examinations, and examinations have also become increasingly important in individual careers.

pmc-12972056.title: Strategies and recommendations for embedding sustainability in innovation and design processes
pmc-12972056.creator: Laura Höpfl, Pascal Dolezalek, Camaren Peter, Alexander Brem, Maria Wirzberger
pmc-12972056.description: The current environmental issues we face are largely due to harmful economic practices. Designing sustainable products and services is crucial for reducing future emissions. Hence, adopting system-oriented models is is essential for encouraging a rethink of current economic and consumption patterns. One important aspect of these approaches is the behavior of consumers, which can be influenced through sustainable product design.

pmc-13080990.title: Pressure-Induced Reduction of Dicyanamide by Samarium(II) in a Coordination Polymer
pmc-13080990.creator: Hannah B. Wineinger, Tyler W. Hines, Kacy N. Mendoza, Thayalan Rajeshkumar, Nicholas B. Beck, Laurent Maron, Joseph M. Sperling, Thomas E. Albrecht
pmc-13080990.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A samarium­(II) coordination polymer, [Sm­(2.2.2-cryptand)­(dca)]­I (dca− = dicyanamide), has been prepared from the reaction of SmI2 with tetrabutylammonium dicyanamide and 2.2.2-cryptand. The structure consists of [Sm­(2.2.2-cryptand)]2+ cations bridged by dicyanamide to form corrugated 1D chains. Single crystals of this compound have been studied spectroscopically using UV–vis–NIR and Raman spectroscopy as a function of pressure to reveal a pressure-induced two-electron reduction of dicyanamide by Sm2+ to cyanide and cyanamide and Sm3+ between 5 and 8 GPa.

pmc-13354356.title: High-grade, poorly differentiated breast carcinoma mimicking primary breast lymphoma: a case report of a diagnostic dilemma
pmc-13354356.creator: Sarada Khadka, Ashish Sapkota, Priyanka Regmi, Rajan Shah, Ishwor Tiwari, Dikshya Thadarai
pmc-13354356.description: Background:High-grade breast carcinomas can occasionally exhibit morphological and immunophenotypic features resembling hematolymphoid neoplasms, leading to diagnostic confusion. Accurate diagnosis is essential to guide appropriate therapy.Case presentation:We report a 35-year-old female presenting with a rapidly enlarging right breast mass. Core biopsy revealed sheets of atypical lymphoid-like cells.

pmc-13367589.title: Prevalence and risk factors of cognitive impairment among geriatric patients at Prince Sultan Military Hospital, Taif, Saudi Arabia
pmc-13367589.creator: Salwa Khalid Abu Asyah, Elham Saad Algethami, Bassam Abdulrahman Alzaidi, Rawan Naif Althomali, Nouf Jafar Alzahrani, Saud K. Alhothaly, Waleed Talal Alsulaimani, Abdullah Ahmed Almalki, Ramy Mohamed Ghazy
pmc-13367589.description: Background:Cognitive impairment and dementia represent a growing public health challenge among the aging population in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of cognitive impairment and identify associated risk factors.Methods:A cross-sectional study was conducted at the Prince Sultan Military Hospital Geriatric Clinic in Taif from November 2024 to May 2025.

pmc-13463913.title: PREHABILITATION FOR PATIENTS UNDERGOING METABOLIC/BARIATRIC SURGERY: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY USING PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHING
pmc-13463913.creator: Yiling YAN, Shengdi LU, Heming WANG, Jiayuan PENG, Lihua HUANG, Yun SHEN, Feng LIU
pmc-13463913.description: ImportanceMultimodal prehabilitation improves outcomes in colorectal surgery, but its effectiveness and cost-effectiveness before metabolic and bariatric surgery are unknown.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a 6-week multimodal prehabilitation programme compared with standard preintervention education in patients undergoing bariatric surgery.Design, setting, and participantsPropensity score matched cohort observational study at Shanghai Tenth People’s Hospital, China, January 2022 to January 2025.

pmc-13519331.title: Longitudinal microcomputed tomography uncovers divergent trajectories of lung maturation in preterm and hyperoxia-exposed neonatal rabbits
pmc-13519331.creator: Davide Buseghin, Erica Ferrini, Martina Buccardi, Giorgio Aquila, Gino Villetti, Chiara Catozzi, Andrea Aliverti, Franco Fabio Stellari, Francesca Pennati
pmc-13519331.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). nderstanding how lung structure and function evolve during the early postnatal period is essential to elucidate the developmental origins of chronic lung disease.1,2 This is particularly relevant in bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), a chronic respiratory disorder of extremely premature infants (<28 weeks gestational age) characterized by arrested alveolarization, simplified distal airspaces, dysmorphic microvasculature, and persistent inflammation or fibrosis, largely induced by perinatal insults such as mechanical ventilation, hyperoxia, and infections.3-5

Animal models are essential to advance our understanding of these processes.

pmc-13573692.creator: Yanxue Lian, Pincheng Luo, Linyi Zheng, Sha Li
